what: Shipped statements with no reading in labs.json yet, each with the row that owes one.
why: Every statement in config/statements is measured on labs and carries a duration, a scanned-byte
reading and an accepted number from an earlier commit. That is the pack docs/design/q1a-runtime-baseline.md
publishes and check:sql-release holds. A statement added while labs cannot be reached has none of
those, and there are only two honest things to do with it: keep it out of the tree until somebody
can log in, or ship it and say plainly that it has no budget.
This file is the second. A name here buys exactly one thing — the recording is allowed not to
mention it — and costs the rest: the gate prints it as unbudgeted, refuses to call Q1 complete
while the list is non-empty, and refuses an entry whose statement has since been measured, so the
list can only shrink. Everything else a statement owes still applies: a declared row bound, a
benchmark class, a descriptor, a reach.
It is not a place to park a slow statement. A measured statement that fails its class ceiling is a
failure, and moving it here would not be allowed: the gate checks that nothing on this list has a
reading.
What the paragraph above got wrong, until row 77: it enumerates what a name here costs and it was
not the whole list. A labs reading is the only thing in this build that parses SQL — the bounds and
grain checks read statements with scan.ts, which says in its own header that it is not a parser. So
an exemption from a measured duration was an exemption from ever being read, and
serving_asset_quality shipped with a missing comma between its two CTEs, failing PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR
where its entry below claims TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND.
So every entry now carries the submission that produced its excuse: the error the platform
returned, the SQLSTATE, the text it returned them for, and what was bound. The gate refuses an
entry whose SQLSTATE is a parse failure, because that is a statement the platform never read, and
one whose statement has changed since. Take a submission with `npm run record:awaiting` against a
bound warehouse. The bindings are placeholders and the record says so: a submission asks whether
the platform read the statement, and no binding makes an absent schema present.
